title: The Havana troupe and the interpreter
summary: He recalls the cast of chorus girls and soubrette, hiring an interpreter, a day off Sunday, and a few Spanish words.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Do you remember who some of these people were? Who was the comedian who went on the tour with you?
Well, it's been so long now, I just can't remember.
What did the soubrette do? What was the function?
She was what we call a star now. She was a star in that particular show then. She sang. A nice-looking person, nice-looking girl. She sang, and always in the limelight sort of thing, you know...
Well, when you were in Cuba, first of all, how did you get along with the language, where the language was concerned?
When we got there, we hired an interpreter to speak the language. He speak the Cuban and American language. So he translated to us what is what, you know.
What about if you wanted to...? First of all, did you have a day off while you were performing? Or were you constantly performing and traveling?
No, we had... In Havana we had one day off. That was Sunday.
Suppose one or two members of the group wanted to go one place and the rest of the group wanted to go somewhere else. What did the interpreter do?

Well, we always... If one person wanted to go to this particular place, whether the rest of them wanted to go or not.... But if they made up their mind to make one trip to (?), all of us would go to one place, you know.
